transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-04
Time: 15:00 PT (42m)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Hiro Tanaka (Ardinex), Sanae Ito (Ardinex), Carlos Reyes (Ardinex)

Auto-summary (auto generated, may be rough):
- Ardinex wants to extend contract 12 months and add a Japan edge region for latency.
- They want a short private pilot (VPC or onprem) to validate p95 latency under marketing peak.
- Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted + burst policy and failover, SSO/SAML, KMS and audit logs.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Maya: hi everyone thanks for joining, um we'll go quick — quick agenda, renewal timing, japan edge onramp and the capacity bump for the campaign.
[00:11] Hiro: thanks maya, yeah, schedule is tight, campaign lands early oct so we need baseline numbers and an onboarding plan sooner rather than later.
[00:18] Sanae: just to add, product wants sub-40ms p95 for tokyo traffic, otherwise the UX hits.
[00:26] Liam: ok sub-40 p95 is doable with an edge region plus some prefix caches, want to cover both hosted edge and a private v-p-c option. fair?
[00:36] Carlos: yeah, and we have compliance constraints, some tokenized data can't leave country, so looking at either Redwood Dedicated in a jp region or Private (onprem/airgapped).
[00:48] Maya: got it — for renewal term, are you thinking 12 months, 24, or a shorter bridge while the pilot runs?
[00:55] Hiro: pref 12 with an option to expand if pilot looks good. also need committed capacity for peak 2x the baseline for 6 weeks.
[01:06] Liam: note on burst: we can set a configurable burst bucket (policy) so you don't overpay but can absorb the 6-week spike. also auto-fallback to a compatible smaller model in case of capacity pressure.
[01:20] Carlos: slight concern — fallback models must not affect output quality for the product. we rely on consistent entity extraction for downstream billing.
[01:29] Liam: yep, can do model rollouts with canary rules and run evals on your prompt set. we can tie quality regressions to rollout thresholds.
[01:40] Sanae: ok, on security: we need SSO (SAML), audit logs retention 1 year, and bring-your-own-kms for key management. is that in scope for the private pilot?
[01:53] Maya: those are standard — SAML SSO and long-retention audit logs are included at enterprise tier, BYO KMS we support for Private and Dedicated. we'll attach the security pack to the pilot plan.
[02:06] Hiro: what about egress costs — particularly if we have a JP edge but some backend services in us-east?
[02:13] Maya: egress flows depend on deployment: hosted edge in jp will minimize egress; if you keep compute onprem we can peer to your VPC to reduce cross-region traffic but edge-to-origin will have typical cloud egress. we'll include estimates in pricing.
[02:27] Sanae: any items that might delay pilot?
[02:31] Liam: potential blockers: onprem firewall rules, KMS provisioning, and a short benchmark window where we need to run 48-72h load to validate p95.
[02:41] Hiro: we can allocate the infra team for that window. Carlos will coordinate.
[02:45] Carlos: yep I'll handle the firewall and networking bits.
[02:48] Maya: great — quick technical deep-dive: Liam, want to walk though the high-level topology?
[02:52] Liam: sure. so option A: Redwood Hosted JP edge — we spin a regional cluster in jp-east, enable prefix caching and kv-cache warm-up, route traffic based on geo. that'll get you sub-40ms p95 for tokyo given normal request sizes.
[03:10] Liam: option B: Private VPC — private control plane, customer-managed vpc peering, bring-your-own kms, and we can run a small onprem inference node inside your tokyo colocation. pros: data residency, full KMS control; cons: slightly more ops and longer lead time.
[03:28] Sanae: what about cost delta? hosted vs private?
[03:32] Liam: hosted is lowest ops and typically lower fixed commitment; Private and Dedicated require a commitment and box-level costs. for burst we can allow limited cross-queue bursting from reserved pools but pricing model differs — will break this out in the sheet.
[03:47] Hiro: micro question — do you support quantization on the edge models to reduce gpu unit costs? we use large model family but can trade off small bits.
[03:56] Liam: yes we support several quantization profiles. early note: quantizashun choices can affect accuracy; we'll propose a middle ground (8-bit with mixed kernels) and include benchmark delta.
[04:09] Carlos: also need to know what kernel/driver matrix you plan to use — we run Ampere GPUs onprem and want to avoid surprises.
[04:16] Liam: we'll include the kernel/driver table, and note any recommended driver versions.
[04:20] Maya: ok moving on to contract specifics — you'll want an amendment for committed capacity for the six-week campaign, plus the 12 month extension. any preferences on invoicing cadence?
[04:30] Hiro: quarterly is fine, with true-up after campaign.
[04:33] Maya: good. I'll propose language for the true-up and burst bill.
[04:36] Sanae: about benchmarks — can we run a smoke test that uses a simplified prompt set before the full 48h stress?
[04:43] Liam: absolutely, two-phase: smoke 4h test, then 48-72h stress test. smoke validates correctness and connectivity; stress validates p95 under load.
[04:53] Hiro: timeline check: if we sign amendment week of 9/13 can pilot start 9/20?
[04:59] Maya: yes, we should be able to hit that if action items complete this week.
[05:03] Carlos: ok i'll get the infra ticket raised and share the list of IP blocks.
[05:07] Maya: on the compliance docs — we'll send SOC2 + ISO artifacts and the private pilot security checklist. are you ok with the standard NDA addendum?
[05:14] Sanae: yes, we'll sign. please include the BYO-KMS diagram.
[05:18] Maya: noted.
[05:20] Hiro: question — any known differences in latency between your Dedicated GPU pools and a private onprem node? we ask because we might prefer Dedicated if the delta is minimal.
[05:30] Liam: Dedicated is close, usually within 10-15% of onprem depending on networking. Onprem can be slightly better for local traffic since no east-west cloud hops. we'll put sample p95 numbers from prior customers anonymized.
[05:44] Carlos: ok that helps.
[05:46] Sanae: competitors — just want to flag GiantCloud AI is pitching a tiered edge that includes a local caches in Tokyo. how do you compare?
[05:55] Maya: common differences — we emphasize production observability and failover (rollouts, evals, token-level cost/latency traces). we'll share a comparison doc but don't get into a long vendor fight here.
[06:09] Hiro: sounds fair.
[06:11] Liam: last technical note — if you plan to run the large model family with continuous batching, KV cache warm starts will save tokens for repeated sessions. we can pre-warm caches during the smoke test.
[06:24] Carlos: that pre-warm idea is great. reduces cost in the campaign week.
[06:28] Maya: ok let's recap next steps and owners: i'll send pricing and pilot plan by wednesday 9/8; liam will share topology and kernel matrix by 9/7; hiro/carlos to provide traffic sketch and IP blocks by 9/10.
[06:43] Hiro: agreed. any other blocker?
[06:46] Sanae: none from product.
[06:48] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and attach the security docs and pricing. end.
